chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: No trouble on the road; the Greenville private club
summary: McRae says bands were welcomed everywhere; they played a private casino club in Greenville, Mississippi.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x:
When you were with
Chick's band, did you have any kind of difficulty
when you were travelling? Things like accommodations
or unnecessary stopping of the bus (inaudible)?

Bands were always welcomed all over
the country, black and white. We never had any
trouble. No trouble -- nothing like that.
People back in those days --
I don't know. Musicians, like I said
before, they were always respected, you know. And

the people was always glad when the bands came in town, because they would have a chance to make some money.
I know a little place in Greenville, Mississippi where we played. We played a big private club.
It was like a -- they had their own casino out there. (Inaudible). These were all private now. Only the rich people could go in this club. They would come from all around.
And they hired Chick Webb to play this club.
And nobody could -- You know, (Inaudible) the millionaires would have these cars. Like casinos. Like everybody got a private casino.
They had gambling, everything in there. Roulette tables, everything. So it was all private. We played there.
